transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees (as captured): Sanjay (AE, Redwood), Maya (SE, Redwood), Evan (Redwood), Alex (Head Infra, Meridian), Priya (Security Lead), Jordan (Product), Samir (Cloud Eng)

Summary:
High-level security posture intake for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and tenant isolation, audit log retention and access, and customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption. Customer also asked about data residency, retention windows for logs and model inputs, and fallback behavior for outages.

Topics covered:
- Compliance evidence: SOC2, ISO 27001, pen test cadence
- Authentication: SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC mapping
- Encryption: at rest & in transit, BYOK/KMS, HSM support
- Auditability: immutable logs, retention, log export to SIEM
- Deployment options: Hosted API, Dedicated instances, Private VPC/on-prem
- Next steps and info/doc requests

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Sanjay (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick round of intros, i'll start — i'm Sanjay, i'll be your AE here and i'll coordinate follow ups. Maya and Evan from infra/solutions will cover technical details.
[00:00:12] Alex: Hi all, Alex here. I run infra at Meridian. We're here to understand security implications before we spin up any pilots.
[00:00:18] Priya: Priya, security lead. i'm primarily interested in evidence for SOC 2 and ISO, how keys are managed and the SSO flow.
[00:00:25] Jordan: Jordan, product. we'll own success criteria on features and retention.
[00:00:30] Sanjay: Great, quick agenda: compliance evidence, auth, encryption/KMS, audit logs/retention, then deployment options — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and we'll capture action items. Sound ok?
[00:00:38] Alex: Yep.
[00:00:40] Maya (SE): i'll try to be as concrete as possible. we do a lot of high-throughput inference, so latency/cost tradeoffs come up a lot but today happy to focus on security.

[00:01:05] Priya: First question — are you SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified? and can we get the attestations and scope? we need to map control owners.
[00:01:16] Sanjay: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, and an ISO 27001 certificate — i'll share the PDFs and the auditor contacts. scope note: hosted control plane and customer metadata are in scope, but for Dedicated/Private some controls shift to the customer — i'll annotate that in the pack.
[00:01:34] Priya: ok that helps. also pen test reports — do you run external penetration tests, and frequency?
[00:01:41] Evan: we do quarterly internal plus annual third-party pen tests; i'll include redacted executive summaries. sometimes findings touch the runtime optimizations, e g, kernel patches for quantized model runtime, we can highlight mitigations.

[00:02:10] Jordan: On the SSO side — we use Okta right now. we need SAML and SCIM provisioning for user groups and RBAC mapping. what does your SSO integration look like?
[00:02:21] Maya: we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. you can map groups from your IdP to Redwood roles. for dedicated/private we also support SAML over internal links in a VPC and SCIM can be routed over a private peering link if required.
[00:02:40] Samir: quick follow — do you support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, and can we require MFA enforced by our IdP?
[00:02:45] Maya: yes both flows; MFA enforcement is handled on the IdP side. Redwood honors the assertion. there is also session management with token lifetimes you can configure.

[00:03:15] Priya: RBAC mapping — we need fine-grained separation between product teams and engineering. can we create custom roles and use resource-level permissions?
[00:03:24] Maya: you can create custom roles, and we support resource-scoped permissions — e.g., model deploy/read/invoke and route-level controls. for Dedicated we add tenancy controls and network isolation. note some lower-level runtime ops still require elevated admin access for debugging; those are logged and auditable.

[00:04:02] Alex: about audit logs — does Redwood provide immutable audit logs? what's retention and can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[00:04:12] Evan: we write audit logs for API calls, admin actions, and model rollout events. for Hosted we retain logs per the plan (default 90 days for standard) but you can export logs to your S3 or push to SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/Logstash integrations. Dedicated/Private can be configured to retain longer and we support longer retention windows and archival to your storage.
[00:04:36] Priya: we need 7 years for some artifacts per our regulatory mapping — is that feasible?
[00:04:41] Sanjay: technically yes, with Dedicated/Private and an archival pipeline you can keep logs for 7 years. hosted plans would be more constrained; we'll call out the cost and storage pattern.

[00:05:10] Samir: about encryption — at rest and in transit, and BYOK. do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM? what's the key wrapping model?
[00:05:20] Maya: we support TLS for in-transit. at rest we encrypt with provider-managed keys by default. for Dedicated and Private we support BYOK using customer KMS — you can bring keys from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and we also have an HSM-backed option for private installs. Key rotation, access controls, and separation of duties are supported. the runtime uses envelope encryption and keys are used for root wrapping.
[00:05:49] Priya: can Redwood access plaintext data? like model inputs stored in cache — is there any way for Redwood personnel to read them?
[00:05:58] Evan: in Hosted, certain operational processes are possible under strict controls, but those require approvals and are logged as part of the audit trail. with BYOK and Private deployment you can restrict decryption keys to your side of the network so Redwood cannot decrypt — that gives maximal isolation.

[00:06:32] Jordan: model outputs and prompts — retention policy question. we process PII in some prompts. can we disable retention or limit it to ephemeral?
[00:06:42] Maya: we offer TTL controls on prompts and responses, and prefixes/KV cache can be configured. for sensitive workloads customers often choose Dedicated/Private and set no-persist or short TTLs. for Hosted we offer data deletion options and contractual terms for retention; we'll include the DPA clauses.

[00:07:10] Priya: regulatory — data residency. our clinical dataset must remain in EU. can you guarantee region pinning for model serving?
[00:07:20] Sanjay: region pinning is supported. for Hosted we have regions and you can request your tenant be pinned to EU. for strongest guarantees Dedicated or Private gives you explicit control over where the workload runs. we'll include the region matrix.

[00:07:48] Alex: does your Private deployment require us to open egress? can it run air-gapped?
[00:07:55] Maya: we have an on-prem package that can be air-gapped for the runtime; control plane options vary — we offer a private control plane that can sit in your VPC with limited egress. certain updates or model provisioning require connectivity unless you opt for fully air-gapped.

[00:08:28] Priya: SOC 2 mapping — do you provide the mapping to controls? we need to tie it to our internal ISMS controls.
[00:08:36] Sanjay: yes we'll provide a control mapping matrix showing which Redwood control maps to common frameworks: SOC2, ISO 27001, and we can align to your policies.

[00:09:00] Jordan: about incident response, do you have an incident playbook and customer notifications, SLA for security incidents?
[00:09:08] Evan: we have a documented IR plan, 24/7 on-call for critical incidents, and we notify affected customers per SLA; for Dedicated/Private we can set up a dedicated escalation channel.

[00:09:32] Samir: curious about network architecture — how are network paths segregated for multi-tenant Hosted? do you use VPC per tenant or logical isolation?
[00:09:42] Maya: Hosted uses logical isolation with network policies and tenant-level encryption. Dedicated spins up dedicated VPCs and private subnets. Private/on-prem is fully under customer control.

[00:10:10] Priya: audit access — who in Redwood can access audit logs and do you have RBAC on the logs?
[00:10:18] Evan: logs are access controlled. we maintain a separate auditing service that supports role-based access. access to raw logs for debugging needs elevated approvals and is logged. we can also stream logs to your SIEM so you control access.

[00:10:45] Alex: two specific asks — 1) can you provide an example SAML metadata and SCIM connector config; 2) a sample retention policy template?
[00:10:56] Sanjay: yes i'll include sample SAML metadata and SCIM mapping remediations. we'll also provide a retention template.

[00:11:15] Priya: liability and breach notif — what are your breach notification SLAs and indemnity posture?
[00:11:23] Sanjay: we'll share the standard terms; early note we have a notification window in our contracts — specifics depend on enterprise legal negotiation. i'll get legal to drop the baseline.

[00:11:40] Jordan: question about model artifacts — do you store customer models or only runtime weights? if we fine-tune any model on our data, where does that live and how's it isolated?
[00:11:52] Maya: we support both: you can host models in our model registry; for private/dedicated you can keep registry on customer-managed storage. fine-tuned models can be stored encrypted in your bucket or in a customer-scoped model registry. access controls apply.

[00:12:20] Samir: operational ops — do you collect telemetry; what's the PII risk?
[00:12:27] Evan: we collect anonymized telemetry for runtime performance; no customer prompt data is used for training unless you opt in. we'll include the telemetry schema.

[00:12:50] Alex: network egress pricing concerns — if we archive logs for 7 years to S3, is there a recommended pattern?
[00:12:58] Maya: recommended: stream logs directly from the runtime to your S3 via our log-shipping connector; for Hosted there's an export cost, for Dedicated you can configure direct connectors to avoid double egress.

[00:13:18] Priya: governance — do you support automated retention enforcement? e g, scheduled purge?
[00:13:24] Maya: yes TTL policies and scheduled purge jobs are supported; we can also sign-off contractually on controlled deletions for sensitive data.

[00:13:45] Sanjay: quick tradeoff summary: Hosted is fastest to onboard but less isolation; Dedicated adds dedicated capacity and tenancy isolation with strong KMS BYOK; Private/on-prem yields the most control including air-gapped options, but higher ops cost.

[00:14:03] Jordan: can Redwood's runtime run in our private subnet with no internet access?
[00:14:09] Maya: yes for on-prem air-gapped we can do that, but updates and model provisioning require an out-of-band process — we provide a package and manual update instructions.

[00:14:30] Priya: we want to make sure privileged ops are auditable and require multi-person approval. is there a privileged access workflow?
[00:14:38] Evan: yes we support step-up approvals and just-in-time privileged access. approvals are logged and retained.

[00:15:00] Alex: can we set contractually that Redwood engineers cannot access certain namespaces without an explicit JIRA ticket and two approvers?
[00:15:10] Sanjay: that's common in enterprise contracts — we'll note it as an option and loop in legal.

[00:15:22] Jordan: on the question of fallback — if a region or capacity fails do you fall back to another region and what about data crossing borders?
[00:15:31] Maya: we have smart routing; fallbacks can be configured but crossing borders is a compliance risk. for regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated with regional capacity or Private to avoid cross-border fallback.

[00:15:50] Priya: audit log integrity — do you support append-only immutable stores or WORM for logs?
[00:15:58] Evan: we can configure WORM-like storage via your archival bucket. for Hosted default logs are managed but we can push to immutable stores on request.

[00:16:20] Samir: about cryptography — what algorithms for envelope encryption and are there FIPS modules/HSM attestation?
[00:16:30] Maya: we use standard AES-256-GCM for data keys and RSA/ECDSA for key wrapping; HSM options provide FIPS 140-2/3 attestation depending on cloud provider.

[00:16:55] Alex: okay last set — we want to run a short pilot. expected traffic maybe 10k requests/day, 95th percentile latency target 250ms, some prompts include PHI. which deployment do you recommend?
[00:17:10] Maya: for PHI and that SLA, Dedicated in EU region with BYOK and short retention TTL is a strong fit; Hosted could work if you contractually restrict retention and pin region, but Dedicated gives clearer guarantees and easier auditability.

[00:17:40] Priya: any SOC2 controls that are not met for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[00:17:46] Sanjay: Hosted inherits all Redwood SOC2 controls but certain controls like customer network isolation and BYOK are only fully realized in Dedicated/Private. we'll highlight which controls rely on customer responsibilities.

[00:18:10] Jordan: price sensitivity — curious ballpark difference between hosted and dedicated for expected volume?
[00:18:18] Sanjay: i'll send ballpark pricing; generally Dedicated has a base monthly commit but lower per-request unit cost at scale. Maya will include an ops/cost estimate.

[00:18:40] (Silence, note: participants reviewing shared doc link)

[00:19:05] Priya: small nit — can we get clarity on your retention descriptors: what counts as 'logs' vs 'customer data' vs 'model artifacts'?
[00:19:14] Evan: logs = API and admin event records; customer data = prompts/outputs and any customer uploaded artifacts; model artifacts = weights and fine-tunes. we'll provide a short definition table.

[00:19:45] Alex: sample legal ask — do you support Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with EU SCCs?
[00:19:53] Sanjay: yes we provide DPA with SCCs as needed. enterprise contracts can include custom clauses.

[00:20:15] Jordan: operational question — in a Dedicated cluster, who is responsible for patching the runtime kernels and ensuring CVE mitigations?
[00:20:24] Maya: for Dedicated we manage the runtime patching but coordinate with you. for Private/on-prem the customer can elect to manage patches; we provide the patches and guidance.

[00:20:55] Priya: curious about data subject requests — can customers execute deletions for specific user-data across logs and prompts?
[00:21:03] Evan: yes, we support targeted deletions and can run a search-and-delete across datasets; for Hosted there is a process and timeframe; for Dedicated/Private you can run deletions directly.

[00:21:30] Sanjay: we're near the halfway mark. want to make sure we capture the asks — i'll summarise: provide SOC2/ISO docs and control mapping, sample SAML/SCIM config, retention template, BYOK/HSM options, dedicated latency/cost estimate, and a proposed pilot plan.

[00:21:55] Alex: yep and we'll provide regulatory retention windows and the compliance questionnaire.

[00:22:10] (brief digression about model quantization and how that affects tokenization — minor mis-transcriptions)

[00:23:00] Maya: technical note: KV cache (may be transcribed as KV cash earlier) is ephemeral unless you configure persistence; we can disable cache persistence for sensitive routes.

[00:23:40] Priya: can we set up path-based routing so certain routes never persist?
[00:23:45] Maya: yes you can set route-level policies to disable persistence and caching.

[00:24:05] Jordan: how do you do developer access and secrets management inside a Dedicated cluster?
[00:24:12] Evan: secrets are stored encrypted via customer KMS if BYOK enabled; developer access is mediated through RBAC and short-lived tokens; we also offer just-in-time elevated access for ops.

[00:24:38] Alex: any references for customers who have done 7-year archival? curious about cost and ops overhead.
[00:24:45] Sanjay: a couple of regulated customers have done that with Dedicated+archival; i'll include anonymized case notes and typical cost bands.

[00:25:10] Priya: can we schedule the follow-up infra deep-dive — ideally with your SE and our cloud eng Samir?
[00:25:17] Maya: yes let's aim for next week — i'll share available slots.

[00:25:35] Samir: also we'd like to run a short POC that includes a simulated breach response runbook test — can Redwood participate?
[00:25:44] Evan: we can do a tabletop exercise; we'll scope it in the follow-up and involve our security folks.

[00:26:05] Jordan: smaller question — for audit log exports, what's the typical format? JSON lines? syslog?
[00:26:12] Maya: we support JSONL, syslog over TLS, and Cloud provider native streams (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Azure Monitor).

[00:26:35] Priya: any constraints on SCIM — group size limits, rate limits?
[00:26:41] Evan: typical SCIM rate limits are in place but configurable for enterprise. we'll note defaults and how to raise them.

[00:27:05] Alex: what about encryption key rotation — can we rotate keys without downtime?
[00:27:12] Maya: yes our envelope pattern supports live rotation; we orchestrate a seamless rotate with a gradual rewrap. we'll share the rotation procedure.

[00:27:40] (participants reference a shared spreadsheet link briefly)

[00:28:00] Sanjay: any open questions we haven't covered?
[00:28:05] Priya: need more on legal posture, but that's ok for now. please include legal contacts and expected baseline contract clauses.
[00:28:12] Sanjay: will do.

[00:28:30] Jordan: schedule a pilot kickoff once we have pricing and SOC docs.

[00:28:40] Sanjay: agreed. i'll send the docs and a first-pass pilot plan.

[00:29:00] (crosstalk, background noise for a few seconds)

[00:29:15] Samir: last quick technical ask — can we get a small network diagram for Dedicated?
[00:29:21] Maya: yes i'll attach a sample VPC topology with subnet examples and NAT/peering notes.

[00:29:40] Alex: and for Private we'll need full on-prem install checklist — hardware, OS, and network pre-reqs.

[00:29:49] Maya: we'll provide the checklist.

[00:30:05] Sanjay: ok everyone's time is precious — i'm going to recap verbally and then we'll email the packet. recap: Redwood will share SOC2/ISO certs, control-mapping, pen test summaries, sample SAML/SCIM configs, retention templates, KMS/HSM options, cost/latency estimate for Dedicated, pilot plan, and sample network diagrams and on-prem checklist. Customer will share compliance questionnaire, retention requirements, Okta metadata, and schedule infra deep-dive.

[00:30:40] Priya: sounds good. one more note — we may request additional logging fields; can you make log schema extensible?
[00:30:47] Evan: yes we can add custom fields or enrich logs with tenant metadata.

[00:31:10] Jordan: cool. we'll aim to review the packet within 5 business days once received.

[00:31:20] Sanjay: great. thanks everyone. i'll follow up with the email and set the next meeting.

[00:31:30] (meeting ends, participants drop)

Notes: transcription contains occasional short mis-hears (KV cash for KV cache, etc.). This transcript is a moderate-fidelity Fireflies export and intentionally retains conversational fragments, interruptions, and some imperfect punctuation.
